Yeah it's a little of both, especially concerning a popular baseball analytics site's WAR for pitchers, which does rely on some (pretty well established) assumptions.  But it's not a perfect stat.  It's still evolving.  And it's not really meant to be summed up and compared on team level.  You'll almost always find a positive correlation between WAR and win percentage, but you'll always find some wacky results too.  Enough that no statistician would ever attempt to project a team's performance on their projected cumulative WAR. One of the problems I have with WAR is that it relies a lot on defense, of course, but defensive metrics are nowhere near reliable at this time of year.  You could have a player with a positive defensive rating and a negative one and his WAR is going to be funky.  And it could remain that way for the whole year, too.  The two have been known to disagree.  Defense is something better analyzed with a LOT of data, and for some positions not even a year's worth of data is a big enough sample.
